newsitem.title: USA: Thorn Apple positive on processed meats.
newsitem.headline: Thorn Apple positive on processed meats.

text.p: Thorn Apple Valley Inc said Thursday the outlook for its processed meats division is to become increasingly profitable based on cost-effective production and a higher-margin product mix.
President Joel Dorfman also said the near-term profitability prospects for the company's Fresh Pork Division are substantially unchanged.
"Recent moves by some of our competitors to reduce industry capacity are encouraging, as are recent reports that breeding intentions are up slightly versus a year ago," he said in a statement.

"Once the imbalance between industry slaughter capacity and the availability of market hogs improves, we expect to be able to deliver significant returns on our investment in this end of our business as well," Dorfman added.

The executive noted that in processed meats, "we have significant unused capacity available as we focus all efforts on increasing volumes in our key product categories. An area that holds particular promise is the export market, especially Korea, Russia and the newly independent states, Mexico, the Caribbean and Japan."

Earlier Thursday, the producer of processed meat and poultry products reported a March 7 third-quarter loss of $0.29 compared to a year-ago loss of $0.63. Sales fell to $205.7 million from $228.8 million.

Sales volume (in pounds) for Thorn Apple Valley's processed meats fell about seven percent as compared with last year's third quarter. Dorfman said the lower volume was "an anticipated result of the company's strategic elimination of lower-margin product lines, especially those that have little potential for margin improvement yet use valuable plant capacities and corporate resources."

Fresh pork sales volume (in pounds) also declined due to a continued industry-wide shortage of market hogs and the company's decision to lower production when incremental costs exceed incremental revenues.
In March, Thorn Apple completed the sale of $17.3 million of nine percent convertible debentures. Proceeds will be used to repay some of the company's secured debt.
